purpose: Store reusable editorial craftsmanship techniques separate from article content, publisher wording, and editorial-policy weights.
boundaries: Do not store article bodies as examples to imitate.
Do not store publisher headline structures or distinctive phrasing as templates.
Store technique, conditions, failure modes, repair results, and measurable craft outcomes only.
Use Story Dossier for facts; use this registry for writing decisions.
techniqueQuestion: Which writing decision made this article pass or fail?

opening.verified_fact_first.name: Verified Fact First
opening.verified_fact_first.principle: Open with the most newsworthy verified fact before context, reaction, or analysis.
whyItWorks: Readers immediately understand what happened.
The Editor can test the lead against the dossier before the article continues.
recognizeBeforeWriting: Dossier has who, what, when, and where.
The first paragraph can be written without publisher phrasing.

structure.intro_body_ending.name: Introduction, Body, Ending
structure.intro_body_ending.principle: Build a full article with a clear lead, supporting body, and closing verified next step.
avoidWhen: brief alerts that only have one verified fact
whyItWorks: It prevents summary fragments from being published as full articles.
It gives the Editor concrete sections to evaluate.
recognizeBeforeWriting: Dossier has at least two supporting facts.
The story can answer what changed and what remains unknown.

transition.fact_to_context.name: Fact To Context
transition.fact_to_context.principle: Move from verified fact to background context before any broader explanation.
useWhen: stories needing history or prior developments
legal, business, policy, and international coverage
avoidWhen: stories where context is still uncertain
whyItWorks: It keeps paragraphs from drifting into unrelated topics.
It reduces generic filler because every transition has a job.
recognizeBeforeWriting: The prior paragraph establishes a fact.
The next paragraph explains why that fact matters in this event.

evidence.classify_before_claim.name: Classify Evidence Before Claim
evidence.classify_before_claim.principle: Know whether each claim comes from an official statement, filing, independent report, eyewitness account, or single-source detail before writing it.
useWhen: court, crime, public safety, political, and business stories
whyItWorks: It separates confirmed facts from developing claims.
It gives the Writer permission to qualify uncertain details naturally.
recognizeBeforeWriting: Dossier labels source tiers.
Single-source details are marked before drafting.

attribution.unique_claim_only.name: Attribute Unique Claims Only
attribution.unique_claim_only.principle: Write shared facts in CE wording and attribute outlet-specific claims only when a detail is not broadly confirmed.
avoidWhen: official-only announcements where the agency is the source
whyItWorks: It avoids over-citing every sentence while preserving traceability.
It reduces copyright risk by not leaning on publisher expression.
recognizeBeforeWriting: Dossier distinguishes consensus facts from unique claims.
A unique claim changes reader understanding.

headline.actor_action_consequence.name: Actor + Action + Consequence
headline.actor_action_consequence.principle: Generate the headline after the article is drafted from the dossier's main actor, action, and consequence.
useWhen: business, politics, sports, local, world, and technology
avoidWhen: stories without a clear actor or confirmed action
whyItWorks: It prevents word salad and publisher-headline imitation.
It keeps the headline anchored to the CE article instead of the RSS title.
recognizeBeforeWriting: Dossier identifies who acted.
Dossier identifies what changed.
A reader can see the consequence in under 12 words.

conclusion.verified_next_step.name: Verified Next Step
conclusion.verified_next_step.principle: Close with the next confirmed action, deadline, official update, or unresolved fact rather than a generic wrap-up.
useWhen: legal, government, public safety, weather, and sports coverage
avoidWhen: stories with no known next step
whyItWorks: It gives readers a concrete reason to return for updates.
It avoids ending every story with the same generic sentence.
recognizeBeforeWriting: Dossier has an unknown, deadline, scheduled update, or official next action.

editorialComments.lesson: Seeded from existing pattern-level learning. Future updates should identify the writing decision behind each pass or failure.

quoteIntegration.claim_context.name: Claim With Context
quoteIntegration.claim_context.principle: Use quotes or reported claims only when they add an actor, evidence, dispute, or official position the article cannot state otherwise.
whyItWorks: It keeps quoted material purposeful and prevents copied article texture.
It supports accountability by linking claims to speakers.
recognizeBeforeWriting: The quote changes what is known.
The speaker or institution matters to the story.

timeline.ordered_developments.name: Ordered Developments
timeline.ordered_developments.principle: Arrange major developments by time so updates add to the original article instead of replacing it with a new generic headline.
useWhen: crime, court, weather, war, politics, and market stories
avoidWhen: stories with only one known timestamp
whyItWorks: It preserves the original CE article while showing what changed.
It helps the Brain detect whether an update is significant enough to republish.
recognizeBeforeWriting: Dossier has original publish date plus at least one later update.

contextPlacement.after_verified_core.name: Context After Verified Core
contextPlacement.after_verified_core.principle: Place background context after the confirmed core facts so the story does not become generic perspective.
avoidWhen: urgent briefs where context would slow the key warning
whyItWorks: It prevents the article from sounding like a template.
It keeps context relevant to the current event.
recognizeBeforeWriting: The core event is already established.
The context explains the current event, not a separate topic.

factOrdering.topic_isolated_sequence.name: Topic-Isolated Fact Sequence
factOrdering.topic_isolated_sequence.principle: Order facts only from the same event cluster and reject paragraphs that introduce facts from a different story.
useWhen: top news, world, politics, business, and local
avoidWhen: roundup newsletters where multiple stories are intentionally separated
whyItWorks: It prevents mixed articles and paragraph-topic contamination.
It lets the Editor repair the earliest drift point instead of rejecting the full article blindly.
recognizeBeforeWriting: All paragraph facts map to the same story id or event cluster.
No unrelated entity appears without a dossier relationship.
